summary: Restoration and mixed land measures dominate Rwanda’s pledges: it cites a 30% forest-cover goal—about 763,440 ha, or 2.3 times the 329,100 ha currently mapped as forest—and plans to rehabilitate over 1,000,000 ha of degraded land by 2030, equivalent to 39% of national land area. Forestry and agroforestry commitments include 47,300 ha of afforestation, 40,000 ha of payment-for-ecosystem-services forest restoration by 2030 (68,460 ha by 2035), and 1,058,920 ha of agroforestry by 2030, rising to 1,469,605 ha by 2035 (about 59–82% of agricultural land). Agriculture targets progressive terraces exceeding 1.1 million ha, crop rotation, mulching, irrigation and improved seeds; the sector is estimated to contribute 5.37 million tCO2e and forestry removals 2.1 million tCO2 in 2035. Conservation expands water-body monitoring to 76 by 2030 and 101 by 2035, contributes to a 30% protected-land target, and raises public green/open space to 30% of built-up areas.
